We’ve had a rest day, so we’ve recharged our batteries. It’s a stage I know very well; my brother and I have come here to train loads of times in this area. I’m very fond of this stage. My home, my village, is just over an hour away from here. So we’re hoping to see lots of people at the start, along the route and at the finish. It’s going to be an interesting and entertaining day because we don’t know what might happen – whether a large breakaway might form or if there’s a team capable of controlling the race on this terrain. After all, the total elevation gain is nearly 3,000 metres. There aren’t any major mountain passes, but it goes up and down all day.
